subject: Business Models
title: Dark Patterns in Cancellation
description: A quick, practical guide to Dark Patterns in Cancellation.

hook.text: To cancel your subscription: call this number, wait 45 minutes, speak to a 'retention specialist.'

buildup.text: Dark patterns are design choices that make it deliberately hard to cancel or downgrade a subscription.

discovery.text: Amazon Prime's cancellation flow had 6 pages and 15 clicks. Signing up took two clicks.

twist.text: The FTC's 'click to cancel' rule now requires online cancellation for any subscription started online.

climax.text: Dark patterns work short-term but destroy trust. Customers who feel trapped become vocal detractors.

punchline.text: Two clicks to join, fifteen to leave. The asymmetry is deliberate.

quiz.question: What are dark patterns in subscription services?
options: Design that makes cancellation deliberately difficult

details.summary: Dark patterns in subscription cancellation are deliberately confusing or obstructive design choices that make canceling unreasonably difficult..
details.whyItMatters: Dark patterns generate short-term retention but long-term brand damage and regulatory risk. The FTC has begun enforcing click-to-cancel rules requiring cancellation to be as easy as sign-up.
takeaways: Deliberately difficult cancellation flows trap subscribers using cognitive friction
Regulators including the FTC are mandating click-to-cancel requirements
Dark pattern retention erodes trust and generates negative brand sentiment

faq.question: What are common dark patterns used to prevent subscription cancellation?
faq.answer: Hiding the cancel option deep within account settings. Requiring phone calls during limited business hours. Presenting multiple retention offers before allowing cancellation. Using confusing button labels where the cancel action is visually de-emphasized. Adding artificial waiting periods.

faq.question: How are regulators addressing subscription cancellation dark patterns?
faq.answer: The FTC's click-to-cancel rule requires cancellation to be as simple as signup. The EU's consumer protection directives mandate clear cancellation processes. California requires online cancellation for online signups. Companies violating these rules face significant fines and enforcement actions.
